title: AI Use and Verification
text:
Starting point
Google Gemini Argon 11/10/2026:
Before using AI for the required extension, briefly state your question, course-based core model, baseline result, and the specific limitation or opportunity you wanted to address.
Our question is about how sleep habits affect the GPA of college freshmen. Our model we made using corse-based material is: term_gpa_i = 3.5138025 + -0.0298120(demo_gender_i) + 0.0216221(bedtime_mssd_i) + 0.0012581(TotalSleepTime_i) + -0.0011879(midpoint_sleep_i) + -0.0019896(daytime_sleep_i) + ε_i. Our baseline results included a Multiple R-squared value of 0.07515, an Adjusted R-squared value of 0.06775, an F-statistic value of 10.16 on 5 and 625 DF, and a p-value of 2.282e-09. Built into the data structure is the fact that no one can get above a 4.0, so there was a cap imposed on the response. Also, in the data the majority of points were between 6-8 hours of sleep, meaning that we had less data points for the extremes. We wanted a solution to improve at least one of these two problems.

title: Analyzing the Relationship Between Sleep Habits and GPA for First-Year College Students
text:
The question
We’re interested in creating a model that will help students understand what sleep habits are associated with higher or lower end-of-term GPA for a first-year university student. In addition to studying total sleep time, we wanted to look at other sleep habit variables such as when students are going to bed (average bedtime) and how much they’re sleeping in the day and how that is associated with GPA. In addition, we wanted to examine the relationship between gender, sleep habits, and GPA to see whether the association between sleep habits and GPA differed by gender.
Our data source is from a study that tracked sleep data and GPA for first-year students at Carnegie Mellon, Notre Dame, and the University of Washington. One limitation is that the data did not come from a random sample of college students, so it may not be representative of the whole population.
